# 1 Maccabees Chapter 12 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 12 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## Council Notes

Chapter 12 contains the famous "Spartans and Jews are brothers" correspondence (vv.5-23), one of the most discussed passages in the book. The claim of Abrahamite kinship between Spartans and Jews is likely a Hasmonean diplomatic fiction, but the author presents it straight. The chapter ends with Jonathan's capture by treachery — a turning point that launches Simon's leadership.

**Key term rulings:**
- "holy scriptures" / "holy books" (v.9) — Greek: βιβλία τά ἅγια; SOPHIA uses "holy scriptures" to match standard English usage
- "council of elders" — consistent with established project terminology for the gerousia
- "Zabadeans" (v.31) — a Nabatean clan; proper name retained
- "Shephelah" (v.38) — standard geographic term for the Judean foothills; retained
- "give them no opportunity to set foot in his territory" (v.25) — key military idiom; retained
- Trypho's treachery (vv.44-48) — the narrative is shaped for maximum dramatic irony; renderings should preserve that irony

---

**1** Jonathan saw that the time was right for him; he chose envoys and sent them to Rome to confirm and renew the friendship that had previously existed between them.

**2** He also sent letters to the Spartans and to other places for the same purpose.

**3** They went to Rome, entered the senate, and said: "Jonathan the high priest and the Jewish nation have sent us to renew the friendship and alliance with you, as it was in former times."

**4** The Romans gave them letters to the local authorities in each place to provide safe conduct to the land of Judea.

**5** This is a copy of the letter that Jonathan wrote to the Spartans:

**6** "Jonathan the high priest, the council of elders of the nation, the priests, and the rest of the Jewish people to their brothers the Spartans, greetings.

**7** Already long ago a letter was sent to Onias the high priest from Arius your king, declaring that you are our brothers, as shown in the copy written below.

**8** Onias received the envoy with honor and accepted the letters, which contained a clear declaration of friendship and alliance.

**9** Although we have no need of these things, having for our encouragement the holy scriptures that are in our hands,

**10** we venture to send to renew the bonds of brotherhood and friendship, lest we become estranged from you; for it has been a long time since you sent to us.

**11** We therefore never cease, at every festival and on other appropriate occasions, to remember you at the sacrifices we offer and in our prayers, as it is right and proper to remember brothers.

**12** We rejoice in your glory.

**13** As for us, many troubles and wars have surrounded us, and the kings around us have fought against us.

**14** We were unwilling to trouble you or our other allies and friends with these wars,

**15** for we have help from Heaven to aid us, and we have been delivered from our enemies, and our enemies have been brought low.

**16** We therefore chose Numenius son of Antiochus and Antipater son of Jason and sent them to the Romans to renew the earlier friendship and alliance with them.

**17** We instructed them to come to you as well, to greet you and deliver to you this letter concerning the renewal of our brotherhood.

**18** Please send us your reply."

**19** This is the copy of the letter that had been sent to Onias:

**20** "Arius king of the Spartans to Onias the high priest, greetings.

**21** It has been found in writing concerning the Spartans and the Jews that they are brothers and are of the family of Abraham.

**22** And now that this has come to light, please write to us about your welfare.

**23** We ourselves write to you: your cattle and your goods are ours, and ours are yours. We command that this be reported to you."

**24** Jonathan heard that the commanders of Demetrius had returned to fight against him with a larger force than before.

**25** He set out from Jerusalem and met them in the region of Hamath, giving them no opportunity to set foot in his territory.

**26** He sent spies into their camp; they returned and reported that the enemy was preparing to attack by night.

**27** When the sun went down, Jonathan ordered his men to stand watch all night, weapons at hand and ready for battle, and he posted sentinels around the camp.

**28** When the enemy heard that Jonathan was prepared and ready for battle, they were afraid, their hearts failed them, and they lit fires in their camp and slipped away.

**29** Jonathan and his men did not know it until morning, for they saw the fires still burning.

**30** Jonathan set out in pursuit but could not overtake them, for they had already crossed the Jordan.

**31** Jonathan turned aside against the Nabateans known as Zabadeans, struck them, and took their plunder.

**32** He broke camp and marched to Damascus and traveled through all that region.

**33** Simon went out and marched as far as Ashkelon and the nearby fortresses, then turned toward Joppa and seized it,

**34** for he had learned that they intended to hand it over to the forces of Demetrius; and he stationed a garrison there to hold it.

**35** When Jonathan returned, he convened the council of elders of the people and consulted with them about building strongholds in Judea

**36** and raising the walls of Jerusalem higher, and constructing a large barrier between the citadel and the city to separate and isolate the citadel from the city, so that it could neither buy nor sell.

**37** They gathered to work on the city; part of the eastern wall had fallen, and he repaired the section called Chaphenatha.

**38** Simon built Adida in the Shephelah, fortified it, and erected gates with bars.

**39** Trypho was now plotting to seize the kingship of Asia, put on the crown, and strike against Antiochus the king.

**40** He feared that Jonathan would not allow this and would go to war against him, so he was looking for a way to seize and kill him. He set out and came to Beth-shan.

**41** Jonathan marched out to meet him with forty thousand picked men of war and came to Beth-shan.

**42** When Trypho saw that Jonathan had come with such a great army, he was afraid to raise a hand against him.

**43** He received Jonathan with honor, commended him to all his friends, gave him gifts, and ordered his troops to obey Jonathan just as they would obey himself.

**44** Then he said to Jonathan: "Why have you wearied all this people when there is no war between us?

**45** Send them home. Choose a few men to accompany you and come with me to Ptolemais; I will hand it over to you, along with the other remaining strongholds, the remaining troops, and all the officials. Then I will turn around and go home — that is why I came."

**46** Jonathan trusted him and did as he said. He dismissed his troops, and they returned to the land of Judea.

**47** He kept three thousand men with himself, leaving two thousand in Galilee while one thousand went with him.

**48** But when Jonathan entered Ptolemais, the men of Ptolemais shut the gates and seized him; all who had entered with him they killed with the sword.

**49** Trypho sent cavalry and infantry into Galilee and the Great Plain to destroy all Jonathan's troops.

**50** But when those men learned that Jonathan had been captured and killed, and all those with him, they encouraged one another and marched in close order, ready for battle.

**51** Those pursuing them saw that they were prepared to fight for their lives, and turned back.

**52** They all reached the land of Judea safely; they mourned Jonathan and those with him and were in great fear; and all Israel made great lamentation.

**53** And all the surrounding nations sought to destroy them utterly, saying: "They have no leader or helper; now let us fight against them and wipe out their memory from among men."
